claims.text: Introducing coherent nanoprecipitates into NiFeCoCr-based high-entropy alloys sharpens the exchange-interaction distribution.
Keeping the nanoprecipitates uniformly smaller than the magnetic domain-wall width enhances the low-field magnetocaloric effect.
Sub-domain-wall-sized coherent nanoprecipitates preserve rapid heat exchange, low hysteresis, and mechanical stability.
The initial NiFeCoCr-based alloy has a predominantly single-phase, disordered microstructure.
High-temperature solutionizing ensures chemical homogeneity.
Controlled aging after solutionizing precipitates coherent nanoprecipitates.
Solutionizing at approximately 1100 °C and aging at around 500 °C for several hours can produce precipitates smaller than the magnetic domain-wall width.
The treatment produces a dual-phase microstructure containing a homogeneous ferromagnetic matrix and uniformly distributed coherent nanoprecipitates.
Coherent nanoprecipitates mechanically reinforce the alloy.
Nanoprecipitates smaller than the domain-wall width do not obstruct magnetic domain-wall motion.
Unobstructed domain-wall motion preserves a uniform exchange field.
The controlled precipitate structure sharpens the magnetic phase transition responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
The controlled precipitate structure reinforces thermal-conduction pathways.
Relative to the single-phase baseline, the treated alloy will have increased refrigerant capacity and a more pronounced magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
Relative to the baseline, the treated alloy will have lower coercivity and hysteresis losses.
Relative to the baseline, the treated alloy will sustain rapid heat exchange and exhibit improved mechanical stability.
The hypothesis applies only where precipitation can be controlled without excessive coarsening.
Large changes in composition or processing that significantly alter diffusion kinetics can place the alloy outside the proposed regime.
Failure of sub-domain-wall-sized precipitates to improve low-field magnetocaloric performance would falsify nanoprecipitate size as the proposed key mediator.
A lack of performance degradation when precipitates exceed the domain-wall width would falsify nanoprecipitate size as the proposed key mediator.
